info.title: eharness team server
info.description: Team-agent server built on eharness (docs/plans/P32-team-example.md). Bearer token auth when TEAM_TOKEN is set; open otherwise.

tags.name: system
tags.description: Health.

tags.name: agents
tags.description: Agent definitions (blueprints).

tags.name: persona
tags.description: The editable persona of an agent: identity, voice, operating rules; versions, proposals and revert.

tags.name: chats
tags.description: Sessions (`eharness/http`): chat thread sessions (`chat:<agentId>:<threadId>`, or `dm:<agentId>` for the first thread of an old agent) and task sessions: stream, resume, interrupt, history. Plus compact, stats and the tools menu of a thread.

tags.name: threads
tags.description: Chat threads per agent, all equal: new chat, rename, archive, and "Discuss in chat" (a new thread seeded with an alert or a run).

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: The bell: urgent alerts and the daily digest (one notification per day).

tags.name: library
tags.description: Shared files: agent artifacts, uploads, version history.

tags.name: artifacts
tags.description: Generated pages, documents, images, diagrams, tables and code with versions, signed content URLs, exports and public sharing (docs/plans/P45-team-artifacts.md).

tags.name: memory
tags.description: Workspace and per-agent memory files.

tags.name: browser
tags.description: Browsers agents drive (docs/plans/P48-browser.md): adapters and their managed runtimes (download, start, stop), profiles with their logins, resource usage, screenshots, and the live view with takeover (a WebSocket).

tags.name: settings
tags.description: Workspace settings read by the agent factory.

tags.name: backups
tags.description: Verified snapshots of the whole database and a readable export of every library and memory file; restore of files (new versions, nothing deleted).

tags.name: storage
tags.description: Where the data directory lives and how big each part is (disk, database, library, backups, scratch dirs), warnings, and owner maintenance actions (compact, checkpoint, retention, clear media).

tags.name: providers
tags.description: Model providers: definitions with their form fields, saved profiles (secrets encrypted, never returned), connection tests and model lists with prices and context windows.

tags.name: routines
tags.description: Scheduled prompts per agent (multi-instance safe, on the durable inbox).

tags.name: programs
tags.description: Standing orders: what an agent does on its own (brief, enforced authority, gates, budget, trigger), with run history.

tags.name: decisions
tags.description: The Decision Center: proposals (a plan or a program), escalations (a parked run asks) and amendments (a run asks for more authority), decided by the client.

tags.name: heartbeat
tags.description: The ambient monitor of an agent (silent unless something needs the client) and the daily digest of what ran, what waits and what it cost.

tags.name: tasks
tags.description: Delegated work across agents (the board).

tags.name: approvals
tags.description: Approvals and questions waiting for a person, across sessions: the list and `POST /attention/{id}/answer`.

tags.name: logs
tags.description: Model call log: every provider call with timing, tokens, cost and payloads.

tags.name: events
tags.description: The feed of changes (`eharness/http` activity): JSON and SSE.

tags.name: developer
tags.description: The Developers page: API agents (isolated agents other applications call), API keys with limits and origins, the request log and usage (docs/plans/P56-developer-api.md).

tags.name: v1
tags.description: The public Developer API, for other machines: `Authorization: Bearer ehk_...`. Mode A runs an agent once, mode B keeps conversations and streams answers in the AI SDK UI message stream format. Errors: `{ error: { code, message } }`.

Bearer.description: The value of TEAM_TOKEN. Not required when the server runs without one.

ApiKey.description: An API key made on the Developers page: `Authorization: Bearer ehk_...`. Only `/v1` accepts it.

boot.description: Id of this server process; it changes on every restart.

enabled.description: `on` / `off` forces it; `inherit` (default) follows the connection: a workspace connection with `defaultEnabled` is available to every agent, an agent's own connection to that agent.

capabilities.description: Mode per capability id ("Read files", "Edit files").

tools.description: Mode per individual tool (Advanced). Rarely needed.

AgentActivity.description: Sidebar data: last message time, its preview and the unread count.

model.description: Model id; null = the workspace default model.

modelProfile.description: Provider profile the model is reached through (with `model` it is the `{ profileId, modelId }` pick); null = the default profile.

toolAccess.description: How the tools of third-party connectors reach the model: `auto` (up front until the agent has 20 or more, then found with `tool_search`) or `on-demand` (always found with `tool_search`); null = the workspace default (`GET /settings`). Built-in connectors are never deferred.

taskConcurrency.description: Assigned tasks (the work queue) this agent works on at the same time; further tasks wait as Queued and start when one ends. Default 1. The team-wide spawn cap (`GET /settings`) still applies.

contextWindow.description: Own context limit in tokens; null = the full window of the agent's current model. Never above the model's window (a larger value is rejected); when the model changes to a smaller window the effective window is the smaller of the two.

compactAtPercent.description: History is summarized when the context reaches this percent of the effective window. Default 80.

connectors.description: This agent's own choices per connection id (on / off / inherit, capability modes). Use `GET /agents/{id}/connectors` for the effective view.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code (eharness codes pass through).

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; derived from the name when absent.

role.description: Default `custom`. The lead exists from the seed.

model.description: Model id. A legacy `profile:model` string is split when the prefix names a profile; a plain id follows `modelProfile`, else the default profile.

modelProfile.description: Provider profile id from `GET /providers`; null = the default profile.

connectors.description: Replaces the whole enablement. Default for a new agent: Files (read only), Memory and Planning. Prefer `PUT /agents/{id}/connectors`.

contextWindow.description: See `Agent.contextWindow`; null = the model's window. Rejected when above the model's window.

model.description: Model id. A legacy `profile:model` string is split when the prefix names a profile; a plain id follows `modelProfile`, else the default profile.

modelProfile.description: Provider profile id from `GET /providers`; null = the default profile.

connectors.description: Replaces the whole enablement. Default for a new agent: Files (read only), Memory and Planning. Prefer `PUT /agents/{id}/connectors`.

contextWindow.description: See `Agent.contextWindow`; null = the model's window. Rejected when above the model's window.

version.description: The `version` the editor loaded; a different current version answers 409 `VERSION_CONFLICT`.

AgentPatch.description: Only the given fields change; `version` bumps.

operatingRules.description: Admin-only operating rules (max 8000 characters); edited here only.

diff.description: Readable diff against the previous version.

displayName.description: How the agent names itself (max 60); empty = the agent name.

about.description: One short line about what it is for (max 300).

language.description: Default answer language (max 40); empty = the language of the person.

request.description: The words of the person that asked, as the agent quoted them.

displayName.description: How the agent names itself (max 60); empty = the agent name.

about.description: One short line about what it is for (max 300).

language.description: Default answer language (max 40); empty = the language of the person.

mode.description: The mode the next tool call runs under. `manual`: risky tools ask a person. `auto`: rules first, then a classifier model allows or blocks (3 blocks in a row or 20 in total pause it and calls ask again). `bypass`: everything runs; deny rules and protected paths still apply.

source.description: `chat`: picked for this chat. `agent`: the agent's own mode. `workspace`: the Settings default.

agentMode.description: The agent's own mode (`inherit` = the workspace default). It is also the loosest mode its sessions may run in: an agent pinned to `manual` cannot be set to `auto` or `bypass`.

available.description: Modes `PUT` accepts now (the agent ceiling and classifier availability applied).

autoAvailable.description: False when the server has no classifier model (an offline scripted model): Auto is not offered.

paused.description: Auto was paused by repeated blocks: calls ask a person until one is approved (or Auto is picked again).

auto.description: Block counters of the live session on this instance.

UiMessage.description: The summary (kind) message; null when there was nothing to compact.

on.description: Offered to the model in this chat.

off.description: Connection ids switched off in this chat (replaces the previous list).

running.description: A turn runs in this process.

profileId.description: The provider profile the model is reached through.

pricing.description: USD per 1M tokens, from the model catalog.

model.description: The model of the agent; no pricing = unknown to the catalog.

activeTurn.description: The turn running anywhere (any instance), or null.

pending.description: Approvals and questions waiting for the user.

turns.description: Turns that ran at least one model step.

sessionId.description: The eharness session of the thread: `chat:<agentId>:<id>`, or `dm:<agentId>` for the thread that existed before threads did. Use it with `/sessions/{id}/…`.

title.description: Null until named: the first message names an unnamed thread.

source.description: Where the conversation lives. `channel` is reserved for messaging channels.

sourceLabel.description: Display label of the source, for example the name of a group.

ref.description: Id of the notification or task.

ThreadSeed.description: What a "Discuss in chat" thread was opened about.

agent.description: Agent id or slug; default the lead.

text.description: Plain short text: what failed, why, and the one next step.

refs.description: App paths that open the evidence or the fix (the first is the primary one).

ackedBy.description: `owner` pressed Ack; `auto` the cause cleared (the next run succeeded, the connection works again).

deliveredAt.description: When it reached the owner (chat message or bell); null while it waits for the rate limit.

chatOff.description: Switched off for this chat only (composer tools menu).

configured.description: What the agent's current activation offers, per connection.

id.description: Id of the call on the Logs page.

lastCall.description: Tools of the newest model call; null when unknown (see the note).

missing.description: Configured and allowed, yet neither loaded nor deferred in the last call: the red flag.

extra.description: Carried by the last call but not configured (plugin tools such as `tool_search`).

name.description: The tool as the agent calls it.

blocked.description: Kept off in this chat because the remote server changed their definitions after the chat first saw them (safety pin). They come back after Accept & reload (`POST /sessions/{id}/reload`). Known from the last turns of the chat on this server; empty after a restart until the chat runs again.

sessions.description: Open sessions the reload looked at.

pending.description: A session is busy: it is closed right after its running turn.

tools.description: Tools the agent is configured with now.

pinsCleared.description: Pinned remote tool definition sets cleared: the owner accepted what the servers offer now. A busy chat is cleared right after its turn and not counted.

running.description: A turn runs, on any instance.

SessionSnapshot.description: The stored state of a session (`eharness/http`).

allOf.description: An AI SDK `UIMessage`. Stored messages carry `metadata.eharness` (turn id, stop reason, usage, pending approvals).

nextBefore.description: Pass as `before` to read older messages; absent = the start.

duplicate.description: The same `Idempotency-Key` was delivered before: nothing was added.

ChatQueued.description: A turn of this chat runs on another instance: the message was stored in the durable inbox and is steered into it. Follow the turn with `GET /sessions/{id}/chat/stream`.

id.description: Chat id of `useChat`; ignored (the chat is the agent DM).

allOf.description: An AI SDK `UIMessage`. Stored messages carry `metadata.eharness` (turn id, stop reason, usage, pending approvals).

messages.description: Only the **last** message is read: a user message (send), or the assistant message with `approval-responded` / `output-available` tool parts (answers a pending approval; the continuation streams into the same message). Ids, metadata and history of the client are never trusted.

messageId.description: With a user message: replace that message and answer it (edit).

target.description: `local`: a turn of this instance was aborted; `remote`: the request was written for the instance running it; `idle`: nothing runs.

AttentionList.description: The library queue, without the app fields of `GET /approvals` (agent name, task, question texts).

id.description: `approvalId`, `toolCallId` (client tool, e.g. a question) or `waitId`: the `{id}` of `POST /attention/{id}/answer`.

agent.description: Slug of the agent that runs the session.

status.description: `recorded`: stored, others of the batch still wait (`remaining`). `resumed`: it was the last one and the session continues server side. `already-answered`: answered elsewhere first (refresh quietly).

reason.description: Shown to the model when denied.

note.description: A free-text note about this call: the model reads it right after the result (approved) or as part of the reason (denied).

remember.description: With `approved: true`: also allow this tool without asking for the rest of the session (and answer the other waiting calls of the same tool in this session at once). With `approved: false`: never allow it in this session.

scope.description: With `approved: true`: how far "always allow" reaches. `session` (default with `remember`): this session. `agent`: a saved rule of this agent, all its sessions. `all`: a saved rule of every agent. Tools a connector pins to ask (writes of third-party connectors) still ask.

answers.description: One answer per question, in order; null dismisses the questions.

answer.description: An approval decision, or the answer of an `ask_user_question`.

lastSeq.description: Cursor for the next call: the `seq` of the last event, else the current head.

resync.description: Present when `after` is older than the events kept by retention: some events were missed, refetch the state (agents, tasks, chats) and continue from `lastSeq`.

TeamEvent.description: App events: `message-added` (agent, role, preview), `task-changed` (taskId, status, pendingKind, title), `agent-message` (from, to, preview), `model-call` (id, kind, status, model; one per logged provider call, for the Logs page) and the change events. Session events come from `eharness/activity` (spec 25): `turn-started` (turnId, kind, source; every turn of every session, also server-started ones), `pending-changed` (a snapshot: `waiting` = approvals / questions that wait for a person, `[]` when nothing does), `approval-decided` (id, approved, by), `attention-answered`, `session-recovered`, `child-reported`.

url.description: Use as the `url` of a `file` part of the next user message; the server resolves it to the file content.

agentId.description: The agent that runs the task session.

parentSessionId.description: The session that delegated the task (the lead DM), if any.

brief.description: Work queue: what to do, in markdown (send-back notes are appended). null for tasks that did not come from the queue.

inputs.description: Library paths the task starts from.

createdBy.description: `client` or the id of the agent that queued it; null = not a work item (no Review step).

acceptedAt.description: When the client accepted the finished work. A done work item with a `done` or `partial` report and no `acceptedAt` is in Review.

round.description: 1, +1 every time the work was sent back.

hold.description: Queued only: the task does not start on its own; the client starts it.

review.description: Finished work waits in Review (client-made tasks by default). false: it goes straight to Done and the creator (an agent) reads the result.

queue.description: Queued tasks only (`GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{id}`): why it has not started. `hold`: held by the client. `worker`: an active worker program of the agent owns the queue. `slot`: the agent (or the team) works on its maximum already; it starts when one ends. `starting`: a slot is free, it starts now.

queueNote.description: Queued tasks only: when a `slot` wait is held by a task that waits for the client, a sentence naming it ("waiting: <task> needs your approval first"). null otherwise.

errorMessage.description: The last error, as the AI provider said it.

running.description: The retry turn runs right now.

retry.description: Only while `status` is `retrying`: the automatic retry of a temporary failure. A task that failed after its last attempt has `status: failed` and no `retry`; `POST /tasks/{id}/retry` continues it by hand.

column.description: Where the board shows the task (`GET /tasks` and `GET /tasks/{id}`). `status` is what the session does; `column` adds what the client sees: a run parked on an open decision (`escalate`, `request_authority`) has `status: running` but `column: waiting`, a finished work item that is not accepted is `review`.

TaskStatus.description: `queued`: in the work queue, no session yet (a worker program takes it); `needs_action`: an approval or question waits for a person; `running` (also while a run is parked on a decision: see `column` of the task for `waiting`); `retrying` (a temporary error, such as an unavailable AI provider, stopped the turn: it is continued automatically at `retry.nextAt`; see `retry`); `done`; `failed`; `stopped` (aborted); `interrupted` (its process stopped; continue it); `timed_out` (a delegation ran past its time limit).

outputs.description: Library paths of what the run produced.

TaskReport.description: The final report of a program run; null for other tasks and while it runs.

attempts.description: 1: checked once; 2: checked again after the one fix-up turn.

DeliverableResult.description: Deliverable checks of a program run; null when the program lists none.

path.description: The path after the tokens were resolved.

TaskGrants.description: Extra permissions given with the task on top of the agent's own; null = none.

allOf.description: An AI SDK `UIMessage`. Stored messages carry `metadata.eharness` (turn id, stop reason, usage, pending approvals).

messages.description: The stored messages of the task session (newest 200).

outputs.description: Library paths of the files the task session wrote, newest first. Filled only with `?outputs=files` (else `[]`); works with `?messages=none`.

chunk.description: The chunk running now (a chunk is up to 80 steps).

steps.description: Model steps of the finished chunks.

costUsd.description: Estimated cost of the finished chunks.

updatedAt.description: Last change (the last checkpoint while running).

stopReason.description: Why a stopped job stopped: `stuck`, `cost`, `duration`, `stopped` (a person) or a stop of the turn.

WorkerJob.description: The long-run job of a background worker task; null for any other task.

id.description: The approval id, or the tool call id of a question: the `{id}` of `POST /attention/{id}/answer`.

answeredWaiting.description: Items of this session that were answered already and wait for the others of the same batch (hidden from the list).

allOf.description: Extra permissions for one task: tool names or rules, connectors (every tool), library path globs to read and to write. Pre-approved on top of what the agent has in chat.

hint.description: What happens next: it starts on its own, waits for a free slot of the agent, or (an active worker program of the agent) is picked up by that program at its next run.

note.description: What to change. Appended to the brief.

pending.description: Approvals / questions waiting in the DM.

delegated.description: Tasks this agent handed to others.

mode.description: `steer` (default): joins the running turn at its next step boundary (a queued turn when idle). `queue`: a turn of its own after the running one.

sessionMode.description: `dm`: the fire is appended to the agent DM chat. `task`: every fire runs in a new task session `routine:<id>:<slot>` (shows on the board).

overlap.description: `skip`: a fire is dropped while the previous one still runs or waits. `queue`: it queues behind.

catchUpWindowMs.description: null: fires missed during downtime are skipped. Else the latest missed slot fires once when it is younger than this.

maxFailures.description: The routine pauses itself at this many.

programId.description: Set when a program owns this routine (the schedule of the program).

RoutineSpec.description: `cron` (5 or 6 fields, IANA timezone, croner syntax), `every` (interval in ms, at least 10 s) or `at` (one shot).

createdBy.description: The agent that wrote the file last; null = a person (an upload or the editor).

ok.description: false while any `error` issue remains: apply refuses.

writes.description: The new library files, with their full text.

finalTarget.description: Where the content ends up after the checks: a library path, `memory:rules.md`, or the archive path. Empty when the row has an error.

originalPath.description: Where the untouched original is kept (the originals folder, or the archive path).

source.description: The memory file, relative to the agent memory root (`notes/ads.md`).

target.description: move: an absolute library path (`/library/knowledge/ads.md`). merge-into: another memory file of this list. Else null.

by.description: Who made the change; null = a person.

ifVersion.description: Omitted: overwrite. `null`: create only (409 `FILE_EXISTS`). A version: write only when the file still has it (409 `VERSION_CONFLICT`, `details.currentVersion`).

kind.description: html, document, image, mermaid, code, data or file (an unknown kind renders as file).

dir.description: The library folder with the files. Empty on the public share page.

shareUrl.description: The public page `<web>/s/<token>`; null while private.

shareVersion.description: null = the public link follows the latest version.

files.description: The files of the current version.

origin.description: Where it came from ("Save as artifact" of a fence in a message).

url.description: Absolute content URL (`/art/v/<id>/<version>/~<token>/<path>`; relative links inside a page keep working). No cookie needed.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms; ask again after it (a 403 means expired).

path.description: A file inside the folder; default: the entry.

visibility.description: private -> public issues a NEW link; public -> private kills it.

shareVersion.description: Pin the public link to a version; null = follow the latest. Public artifacts only.

ifVersion.description: The library version of the entry file you edited (`GET /library/file`). A stale edit gets 409 `VERSION_CONFLICT` (`error.details.currentVersion`).

entryUrl.description: Public content URL of the entry file (CORS open, no login).

baseUrl.description: Public content URL prefix of the folder; append a relative file path.

defaultPermissionMode.description: The workspace default permission mode: `default` = Manual, `auto` = Auto (classifier), `bypassPermissions` = Bypass. The mode of every chat and agent that has none of its own; read on every tool call.

toolAccess.description: Tool access of agents without their own setting: `auto` or `on-demand` (third-party connector tools found with `tool_search`).

toolWarmDays.description: Tools an agent called in the last this many days load up front instead of being found with `tool_search` (a discovery resets the prompt cache). 0 = off. Default 7.

budgetUsd.description: Monthly USD limit of the workspace budget ledger; null = tracked, not limited.

spawnCap.description: Children the lead runs at once (`subagents` `maxConcurrent`).

defaultModel.description: Model id of agents without their own; null = the default model of the default profile.

defaultProfile.description: Provider profile of agents without their own pick; null = the server default (the env profile, else the first enabled one).

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the team (default: the `TZ` variable or the host timezone). The default of the heartbeat active hours and of the daily digest time; an agent heartbeat or the digest can override it.

stuckRunMinutes.description: A program, routine or queued run with no activity for this many minutes is stopped through the Stop path and raises an alarm (Health, Needs attention). It is never run again by itself. Default 45.

classifierModel.description: Model of the Auto mode classifier. null = "Same as the agent": the model of the agent whose action is judged. The initial value is `TEAM_CLASSIFIER_MODEL` when set.

classifierProfile.description: Provider profile of `classifierModel`; null = the workspace default profile.

searchModel.description: Model of `web_search`. null = the built-in small model of the provider. The initial value is `TEAM_SEARCH_MODEL` when set.

searchProfile.description: Provider profile of `searchModel` (an OpenRouter or AI Gateway profile); null = the workspace default profile, else the first that can search.

contextCap.description: Deprecated ceiling on every agent context window (tokens). null = none: the window follows each agent model. Initial value: `TEAM_CONTEXT_CAP`.

heartbeatContextWindow.description: The working context window (tokens) of every heartbeat session, independent of the chat window of the agent and clamped to its model window. History is summarized early so each beat starts small. Default 64000.

connectorHealthTtlMs.description: A custom connector is re-checked in the background when its last check is older than this (ms); 0 = on every listing; null = never. Default 60000.

connectorProbeRetryMs.description: A failed check of a connected server is retried once after this long (ms) before the connection counts as down. Default 3000.

longRunMaxCostUsd.description: A background worker job stops at this estimated cost (USD); 0 = no limit. Default 10.

longRunMaxHours.description: A background worker job stops this many hours after it started; 0 = no limit. Default 24.

longRunChunkSteps.description: Steps per chunk of a background worker job. Default 80.

maxRepeatingReminders.description: Most active repeating reminders one person may have; 0 = no limit. Default 10.

teamName.description: The team name given to agents in chats; null = none. Initial value: `TEAM_NAME`.

worksRoot.description: Library folder of the daily works journal: agents append follow-ups and notes to `<folder>/YYYY/MM/DD.md` (team timezone). Default `/library/works`.

companyRoot.description: Library folder that holds the company files (for example `/library/acme`): agents are told to keep company facts, knowledge, reports and ledgers under it (`knowledge/`, `reports/`, `data/`, `kpi/`, `attendance/`). null = the built-in folders (`/library/company`, `/library/knowledge`, `/library/reports`, `/library/data`). Changing it moves no file.

eventsRetentionHours.description: Events feed: hours kept; 0 = by count only. Default 72.

logMaxRows.description: Model call log (Logs page): rows kept. Default 5000.

logRetentionDays.description: Model call log: days kept. Default 7.

logBodyHours.description: Model call log: hours the full request and response are kept; older calls keep metadata only (tokens, cost, timing). 0 = never keep them. Default 24.

mediaRetentionDays.description: Tool media and browser screenshots kept this many days; 0 = keep. Default 3.

routineRunsRetentionDays.description: Finished routine runs kept this many days; 0 = keep. Default 30.

tasksRetentionDays.description: Finished tasks kept this many days; 0 = keep. Default 90.

libraryHistoryRetentionDays.description: Library history kept this many days; 0 = keep. Default 180.

backupEnabled.description: Automatic backups: a snapshot every day at `backupTime` and one at start-up when none was taken today. Default on. Manual and before-risky-operation snapshots always work.

backupTime.description: Local time (team timezone) of the daily snapshot, HH:MM. Default 02:00.

backupKeepDaily.description: The newest snapshot of each of this many days is kept. Default 14.

backupKeepWeekly.description: The newest snapshot of each of this many weeks is kept. Default 8.

workspaceDefault.description: What an agent without a model of its own runs on; null when no provider is configured.

modelId.description: null: follows the model of each agent.

source.description: `setting`: picked in Settings or on the agent; `env`: from `TEAM_MODEL`; `built-in`: the provider fallback nobody chose; `agent`: follows the model of each agent.

agentsOnFallback.description: Names of agents that run on a built-in fallback model because none was picked.

python.description: Python version of the interpreter; null when off, unknown or inside docker.

isolated.description: True when the code runs under an OS sandbox or in a container, without network.

remote.description: The Remote sandbox connector when one is connected (host of its URL, never the token); null when it is not reachable.
The connected Remote sandbox that can host managed Chrome profiles.

running.description: Ids of profiles with a running engine.

error.description: Why the last download or start failed.

where.description: `remote`: the engine of the connected Remote sandbox (its `adapter` is `<adapter>@remote`, usable in `/browser/runtimes/{adapter}`). Absent: this server.

host.description: Host of the Remote sandbox (`remote` only).

defaultModel.description: A model id, or the legacy `profile:model` (split when the prefix names a profile).

pausedAt.description: When the pause began (ms); null = running.

holdChannels.description: Inbound chat messages are kept but do not wake an agent (answered after Resume only with `answerHeldOnResume`).

answerHeldOnResume.description: Resume answers the held chat messages that addressed the agent (at most 12 hours old), once per conversation.

held.description: What is active now and would fire if the workspace ran.

skippedWhilePaused.description: Runs skipped with reason 'paused' since `pausedAt` (0 when not paused).

answerHeldOnResume.description: Answer the held chat messages after Resume (default false; pausing again keeps the choice).

stopRunning.description: Stop agent runs that are running now (default false: they finish).

dir.description: `TEAM_BACKUP_DIR`, else a folder in the OS temporary directory (cleared on a container restart).

temporary.description: The backups are in temporary storage: download a backup to keep it.

stale.description: No verified snapshot exists, or the newest is older than 36 hours.

filesBytes.description: Size of the workspace export (zip); null = none.

fileCount.description: Library and memory files in the workspace export.

verified.description: `PRAGMA integrity_check` of the copy answered `ok` and its row counts of library files and agents matched the live database.

post.summary: Send a message, answer an approval or regenerate (useChat)
post.description:
`eharness/http` (spec 26 §5). The body is an AI SDK `useChat` request; the response is the UI message stream (`text/event-stream`).

- **Send**: the last message is a user message. Attachments are `file` parts (`data:` / `https:` URLs, or the `library:///uploads/…` url returned by `POST /library/files`; media type and reference are checked here).
- **Approvals**: a client that posts the assistant message back with the part in `approval-responded` continues into the **same** message id (the web app answers through `POST /attention/{id}/answer` instead). A message none of whose answers is waiting any more is `409 EH_HTTP_ALREADY_ANSWERED`.
- **Regenerate / edit**: `trigger: "regenerate-message"`, or a user message with `messageId`.
- **Idempotency**: the `Idempotency-Key` header, else the user message id; a repeat is `409 EH_HTTP_DUPLICATE_REQUEST` (with `details.active` and the turn).

Busy policy (`?ifBusy=`, default `steer`): while a turn of this chat runs, a new user message is **steered** into it: on this instance the response follows the running turn; when another instance runs it the message goes through the durable inbox and the route answers `202`. `reject` answers `409 EH_SESSION_BUSY`. Approvals, regenerate and edit never steer: `409`.

Only DM sessions take chat (a task takes messages through `POST /tasks/{id}/messages`: `409 TASK_SESSION`); an archived agent answers `409 AGENT_ARCHIVED`. Errors after the turn started arrive as an `error` chunk inside the stream.

`eharness/http`. `respond()` on the session that owns the item, from whichever instance receives the request. A step can raise several approvals at once: each answer is recorded on its own (`status: "recorded"`, `remaining` = items still waiting) and the answer to the last one resumes the session (`status: "resumed"`). Nothing streams: the continuation runs server side and shows in the activity feed.

- Approval: `{ kind: "approval", approved, reason?, note?, remember? }`. `remember: "session"` grants the tool for the rest of the session. `note` is shown to the model after the result.
- Question: `{ kind: "question", answers }` (one per question, `null` dismisses).

An item that is gone is `404`; answered elsewhere first is `200 already-answered`; a running turn is `409`.

The answer's `uploadId` is the source of the preview and the import.

Compares the zip with the workspace, entity by entity: `added`, `changed` (with a readable diff for text and the changed fields of JSON), `unchanged` (only counted), `only-live` (kept: an import never deletes unless a section is ticked for removal). Each item lists what applying it would grant (`authority`: permission mode, tool rules, connector enablement, program authority, directory roles). Connections and reminders are reference only. Ids are kept for matched entities (agent slug, program name per agent, library path, routine id then name, person id then name); new ones get new ids; references are remapped. An item that exists here and differs is skipped unless `selection.overwrite` is true (an undo always overwrites). Secrets come back only from the encrypted `secrets.enc.json`, when `selection.sections` includes `secrets` and the `passphrase` is right (a wrong one answers 400 `IMPORT_PASSPHRASE` and nothing is applied). Server to client:
- text `{ "type": "hello", "profileId", "info": { "width", "height", "liveView", "liveUrl"? }, "controller": { "by": "agent"|"human", "holder"?, "since", "reason"? }, "you": { "id", "canTakeOver": boolean } }` once.
- binary frames: 4-byte big-endian header length, JSON header `{ "type": "frame", "seq", "width", "height", "mediaType": "image/jpeg"|"image/png", "at" }`, then the image bytes. Coordinates of `input` events are in the `width` x `height` of the frame.
- text `{ "type": "controller", "controller": {...} }` whenever who drives the browser changes (a person took over, handed back, or the agent asked for a person).
- text `{ "type": "ack", "id", "ok": boolean, "error"? }` for a command that carried an `id`; `{ "type": "error", "message", "id"? }` for a refused input or command.

post.summary: Mode A: run an agent once
post.description:
One-shot: send an input, get an answer. Nothing is stored except metadata (time, key, tokens, cost). With `outputSchema` the answer is validated JSON.

```bash
curl -X POST $BASE/v1/agents/support-bot/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EHARNESS_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"Where is order 1042?","context":{"customer":"Acme"}}'
```

post.summary: Send a message; the answer streams
post.description:
Default: Server-Sent Events in the AI SDK UI message stream format, so `useChat` (`DefaultChatTransport({ api })`) and `eharness/client` can read it. The body may be `{ text }` or what `useChat` sends (`{ messages }`: the last user message is used). With `"stream": false` (or `?stream=false`) the answer is one JSON object.

```bash
curl -N -X POST $BASE/v1/conversations/$ID/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EHARNESS_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hello"}'
```

200.description: A UI message stream, or JSON when `stream` is false

schema.description: Server-sent events in the AI SDK UI message stream format (`text-delta` chunks, then `[DONE]`). Tool calls and reasoning are never sent.
